title: A Chennai port terminal just set its highest container record in a decade. November 7, 2026.
excerpt: From a scientist who noticed why the sea looks blue and won India's first Nobel in science, to a Mumbai-born engineer now leading a US nursing school, to a Chennai port breaking its own record twice in two months, to a Bihar homemaker now advising 400 farmers - November 7's four stories are about curiosity and persistence compounding into something much bigger.
bodyHtml:
Every story today starts small - a question about the sea's color, an engineering degree repurposed, a single terminal's monthly numbers, one woman's 21-day course - and ends up somewhere much larger.

He noticed why the sea looks blue - and became the first Asian ever to win a Nobel Prize in science

Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman was born November 7, 1888, in Tiruchirappalli. In 1930, he won the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering the Raman Effect - how light scatters through a transparent material, revealing its molecular structure - still used today in chemistry and medical diagnostics.

She was born in Mumbai, trained as an engineer. In 2026, she became dean of a top US nursing school

Dr. Kavita Radhakrishnan became permanent Dean of UT Austin's School of Nursing on September 1, 2026. Mumbai-born, she earned an electronics engineering degree before pivoting to nursing science, now holding over $10 million in NIH research funding.

A Chennai port terminal just set its highest container record in a decade

Chennai Container Terminal, operated by DP World, reportedly handled 93,804 TEUs in October 2026 - its highest monthly throughput in a decade, beating its own prior record set just one month earlier.

She was confined to her home until a few years ago. Now 400 farmers come to her for advice

Shobha Devi, from Tikha village in Muzaffarpur district, Bihar, joined a Jeevika self-help group in 2020 and built an Agri-Entrepreneur Service Centre around mushroom cultivation and organic farm inputs - now advising roughly 400 farmers on soil health and pest management.

Four stories, one pattern: a question about the sea that won a Nobel, an engineering degree that became a dean's office, a port that broke its own record twice running, and a homemaker who became an advisor to hundreds.
